subject: Inference cost pressure & pilot qualification — synthesis
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara@aisha-systems.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Inference cost pressure & pilot qualification — synthesis

Hi Sara — thanks again for taking the time today. Below is a concise recap so we have alignment on pain, success criteria, and next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

TL;DR
- Main problem: unit token cost variability + high median token cost when serving LLM-based ranking/classification at scale.
- Goal: validate a production pilot that reduces per-token inference cost 2x (target) while keeping 95th%-tile latency under 200ms for short-turn prompts and no more than 1.5% quality regression on your evaluation set.

What we heard (pain points)
- Monthly inference spend has grown ~3x YoY; biggest driver is hallucination-driven re-requests and naive single-request routing.
- Current stack: self-hosted Sagemaker endpoints (p3/p4), bespoke batching layer, and Redis for session storage. No prefix caching.
- Ops pain: unpredictable bursts from nightly re-rank jobs and heavy morning traffic; manual scaling is slow and expensive.
- Risk posture: data residency requirements, but you are comfortable with hosted service if data retention & encryption controls are explicit.

Success criteria for a pilot
- Target unit cost reduction: 1.8–2.5x (we recommended planning for 2x).
- Latency SLO: p95 < 200ms for the 0.5–2s prompt class; p99 fallback acceptable if documented.
- Quality: automated eval against your 10k prompt set with <1.5% F1 degradation (classification) or <2% BLEU-style drop for short-generation tasks.
- Operational: weekly cost + latency dashboard and one rollback policy.

Technical approaches we sketched
- Smart batching + continuous KV cache for identical prefixes (expect the biggest wins on re-rank jobs).
- Quantization exploration: run controlled int8 evals with a held-out prompt set; fall back to fp16 where quality is impacted.
- Model routing: cheaper model for lower-criticality requests; route heavy-context requests to a higher-capacity variant.

Next steps (agreed)
1) You to share 2 sample days of traffic (CSV) and a small eval seed (50–100 prompts with labels) — we can use anonymized samples. (Sara to send)
2) We share a Redwood cost model template and a pilot scope doc for alignment (Logan -> attached).
3) Quick SE sync to validate batching and cache integration details (schedule with Priyom).
4) Target pilot kickoff week: 2027-05-17 (tentative) — pilot duration 4 weeks.

Attachments: pilot-scope-outline.pdf, aisha-throughput-sample.csv (placeholder you can overwrite)

If that all looks right, I’ll open the HubSpot deal and send calendar invites for the SE deep-dive.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Enterprise Account Exec | Redwood Inference
logan_wright@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Sara Lin <sara@aisha-systems.com>

Cc: Aisha Systems Procurement <procurement@aisha-systems.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T19:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inference cost pressure & pilot qualification — synthesis

Thanks Logan — this is a very helpful summary and aligned with what we discussed. A few clarifications and answers below.

Clarifications
- Attachments: I’m attaching a short sample of our throughput export for 2027-04-01 to 2027-04-02 (anonymized). It contains request timestamps, prompt length, and issued retries.
- Quality tolerance: for our production ranking pipeline, staying within 1% F1 is preferred, but 1.5% is acceptable if the cost savings are substantial.
- Quantization openness: our ML team is open to int8 evaluation but we require a small validation harness and side-by-side outputs to sign off.
- Data residency: we need explicit data retention of 30 days for logs and 90 days for audit traces; KMS integration is a must.

A couple of asks
- Can you add an expected ballpark of cost per 1M tokens for the proposed pilot configuration (even a rough estimate) so I can prep procurement?
- In the pilot scope, include the exact metrics we’ll expose (token cost, p95 latency, eval F1, cache hit rate).

I’ve looped in procurement for visibility. We’ll upload the CSV to the Drive link you shared by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Sara Lin
Head of ML Platform | Aisha Systems
sara@aisha-systems.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara@aisha-systems.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inference cost pressure & pilot qualification — synthesis

Hi all — quick technical follow-up after reviewing the sample throughput export Sara mentioned (thanks in advance for uploading). A few concrete notes from an SE perspective: 

1) Batching and cache expectations
- Based on the sample distribution Logan summarized, we should be able to achieve ~1.6–2.1x effective token cost reduction from batch consolidation + prefix/KV caching on re-rank jobs. This assumes a median prompt length < 256 tokens and ~15% identical-prefix reuse across requests.
- Implementation options: (a) integrate Redwood SDK for automatic request grouping (minimal code change), or (b) use a sidecar proxy that aggregates at the network edge (lower code change but operationally heavier).

2) Quantization plan
- Proposal: run a parallel eval run on your seed prompts with the model quantized to int8 (post-training quantization with per-channel scales) and compute delta metrics. We will keep an fp16 baseline. Expected risk: for classification tasks we often see <1% performance regression; for short generative outputs risk is higher.

3) Data & security
- Redwood Private options give you the KMS/HSM integration and 30/90 day retention configuration. We’ll include audit logs for every inference request in the pilot.

4) Pilot instrumentation
- We’ll provide dashboards for token-level cost, p95/p99 latency, cache hit rate, and per-route quality regression alerts. We’ll also produce a weekly readout doc.

Action items I can own this week
- Load a starter cost projection into the attached redwood-cost-modeling-template.xlsx and share a populated version by Friday.
- Draft a short eval harness script (Python) to run int8 vs fp16 on the 100-sample set once provided.

If that sounds good I’ll propose 30–45 minute SE deep-dive slots next week to align on integration approach.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Inference cost pressure & pilot qualification — synthesis

Great — thanks for the rapid responses and for looping procurement. Short confirm and calendar items: 

Confirmed pilot scope (one-line)
- 4-week pilot to validate 2x unit-cost reduction target via batching + KV caching and an int8 quality sweep on your 100-sample eval set.

Confirmed success metrics
- Unit cost: >=1.8x improvement target (we’ll report per-1M-token projection).
- Latency: p95 < 200ms for short prompts.
- Quality: <=1.5% F1 drop on ranked outputs (1% preferred).
- Operational: cache hit rate reporting and a rollback policy if quality is >2.5% off baseline.

Next calendar steps
- Priyom to propose SE deep-dive slots (I asked for Wed/Thu next week).
- Sara to upload anonymized CSV + 100-sample eval to the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-pilot-Aisha (Procurement will receive the cost projection).
- Logan to share populated cost model by Friday and an initial SOW stub for procurement review.

Closing ask: Sara — if procurement wants a ballpark per-1M-token number for inclusion in the purchase request, our rough pilot estimate (pre-quant/with conservative hit-rate) is $450–$650 / 1M tokens. We will refine once we run the pilot projection.

I’ll update the HubSpot deal and send the invites once Priyom posts SE slots. Thanks all — looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
